answers.title: Undo a change you already pushed
answers.markdown:
## Undo a change you already pushed

Don't rewrite history that someone else may have pulled. Add a new commit that does the opposite:

```sh
git log --oneline            # find the commit to undo
git revert --no-edit HEAD    # or: git revert <commit>
git push
```

`git revert` leaves the history intact, so everyone can still see what happened and when. If `main` is protected, do this on a branch and open a pull request.

**Never** `git push --force` on a shared branch to get rid of it.

answers.title: Undo a commit you haven't pushed
answers.markdown:
## Undo a commit you haven't pushed

Nobody else has it yet, so you may rewrite it:

```sh
git reset --soft HEAD~1   # undo the commit, keep the changes staged
git reset --hard HEAD~1   # undo the commit AND throw the changes away
```

Check first with `git log --oneline`: if the commit is already on the server, use `git revert` instead.

answers.title: Throw away changes in a file
answers.markdown:
## Throw away changes in a file

```sh
git status                  # what changed
git restore <file>          # discard edits you haven't staged
git restore --staged <file> # unstage it, keep the edits
```

Discarding is permanent: there is no undo for edits that were never committed.

answers.title: Make or switch branches
answers.markdown:
## Branches

```sh
git switch -c my-change     # make a new branch from where you are, and move to it
git switch main             # go back to main
git branch                  # list branches (* marks the current one)
git push -u origin my-change   # first push of a new branch
```

Start every change from an up-to-date `main`: `git switch main && git pull`, then branch.

answers.title: Why I can't push to main
answers.markdown:
## Why you can't push to `main`

`main` is protected on purpose: changes reach it through a pull request, with a passing check and a review.

```sh
git switch -c my-change     # move your commit to a branch
git push -u origin my-change
```

Then open the pull request in Forgejo. If you already committed on `main` by mistake: make the branch first (above), then `git switch main && git reset --hard origin/main`.

answers.title: Get the latest changes
answers.markdown:
## Get the latest changes

```sh
git switch main
git pull                    # fetch and merge what others pushed
```

On a branch that's behind `main`: `git pull origin main` brings `main`'s commits into it. Resolve any conflict, commit, push.

answers.title: Fix a merge conflict
answers.markdown:
## Fix a merge conflict

Git stopped because two changes touched the same lines. It marked the file:

```text
<<<<<<< HEAD
your version
=======
their version
>>>>>>> other-branch
```

1. Open the file, keep what's right (yours, theirs or both) and delete the three marker lines.
2. `git add <file>`
3. `git commit` (or `git merge --continue` / `git rebase --continue` if you were in one)
4. `git status` should say the tree is clean.

answers.title: See what I changed
answers.markdown:
## See what you changed

```sh
git status             # which files changed, and what is staged
git diff               # edits not yet staged
git diff --staged      # edits that will go in the next commit
git log --oneline      # the history
```

answers.title: Fix my last commit message
answers.markdown:
## Fix the last commit message

```sh
git commit --amend -m "better message"
```

Only if you haven't pushed it. If it's already pushed, leave it: rewriting shared history causes more trouble than a typo.

answers.title: Get a copy of a repo
answers.markdown:
## Clone a repo

```sh
git clone http://git-server:3000/<owner>/<repo>.git
cd <repo>
```

Your terminal is already signed in to the Forgejo server, so no password prompt.
